purpose: Clarify what the 18 loss-legacy matched pairs biologically represent before any hydrodynamic outcome exists.

loss_legacy_history.interpretation: Most recent qualifying focal-loss events more often represent persistence of an already co-occurring alternative seagrass through Thalassia dropout than de-novo post-loss colonization.

current_alternative_only_persistence.interpretation: The full 18-pair cohort must not be described as 18 established long-term replacement states. For most points, the current Thalassia-absent alternative-only state is recent.

persistent_thalassia_comparator_composit.interpretation: Most persistent-Thalassia comparators are mixed canopies, so the matched primary is not a simple pure-species comparison.

revised_ecological_framing.preferred: history-linked focal-foundation-species dropout within still-vegetated meadow states
revised_ecological_framing.stronger_mechanistic_candidate: pre-existing community insurance: an alternative canopy already present before focal loss may preserve occupancy and possibly physical function after Thalassia dropout
avoid: succession from Thalassia to an alternative species
post-loss colonization as the general mechanism
pure Thalassia versus pure replacement-species experiment

inferential_rule.primary_unchanged: Use all qualifying matched pairs under the already frozen history-linked attenuation primary.
inferential_rule.history_depth_role: History depth, pre-existing-alternative status, and comparator mixture are descriptive scope/transportability diagnostics only.
no_rescue: Do not restrict the primary to >=2-year or >=3-year alternative-only runs after seeing attenuation.
Do not promote the 13 pre-existing-alternative pairs to a new confirmatory primary after seeing attenuation.
Do not treat mixed comparator composition as an exclusion criterion after seeing attenuation.
Any future persistence-duration or pre-existing-versus-new-alternative interaction requires a separately powered prospective design.
